title: Spread of Chinese culture to Korea, Japan and Vietnam
summary: Han China's expansion under Emperor Wu reached the regions of modern Korea and Vietnam. Over the following centuries, Chinese ideas took root in neighbouring states. Later Confucian thinkers Zhu Xi and Wang Yangming had tremendous influence in Korea, Japan and Vietnam, and a great deal of Confucian debate in East Asia is still framed by the schools they shaped.

uncertainty.note: Spread intensified with Emperor Wu of Han's campaigns into northern Vietnam (111 BCE) and the Korean peninsula (108 BCE), with institutional and philosophical synthesis flourishing through the Tang, Song, and early modern eras.

importance.justification: Chinese learning and thought shaped states across East Asia.

reviewer_note: These sources show only part of this spread, and do not cover script, Buddhism or law in detail. Local states adapted these ideas. Dates are approximate, and the pin at Xi'an is a stand-in.
